title: CHARACTER concatenation A // B keeps both fields' trailing blanks — TRIM is non-standard pre-F90
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE BUILD_PATH(DIR, FILE, FULL)
C     DIR is CHARACTER*16, FILE is CHARACTER*16. The concatenation
C     DIR // '/' // FILE produces a 33-character string where DIR
C     occupies the first 16 (padded with blanks) -- the result
C     looks like 'home            /report.txt     '. TRIM(DIR) (F90+)
C     fixes this; in pure F77 the workaround is to track the
C     'real' length manually with INDEX or LEN_TRIM.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*16 DIR, FILE
      CHARACTER*33 FULL
      FULL = DIR // '/' // FILE
      END
notes: Path-building (or any string concatenation) over fixed-width CHARACTER usually wants TRIM or LEN_TRIM. Pre-F90 code that doesn't have TRIM available uses INDEX(STR, ' ') as a workaround. The spec must capture the trim-or-pad intent so the port preserves it.
